## generic_dense_select_gen3

**Finding type: suspected shortcut.** Audited generator SHA-256: `82f27ec2303a759ab646f81910024bcbbdba448eb00b60334bfc01e27e0d0953` (version 1.1.0).

The documented rule is “keep the unique shape,” but the generator always chooses `odd_size != base_size`. Therefore a weaker rule—**keep the only object whose cell count is unique**—makes the same prediction on generated data without representing shape equivalence.

I sampled seeds 0–499 in each of easy/medium/hard: 1,500 generated tasks, 7,461 labelled pairs, and 7,274 unique inputs. Every pair had exactly one shape singleton, that same object was also the only size singleton, and the size-only rival matched all 7,461 saved outputs. Exact counts, source binding, script, and failures list are in `checks/audit/generic_dense_select_gen3/report.json` and `probe.py`.

`checks/audit/generic_dense_select_gen3/input.json` is a concrete same-size counterexample: three translated L triominoes and one horizontal triomino, all size three. The intended Python `_apply` keeps the horizontal triomino; the size-only rival finds no unique size and returns the input. Outputs are in `python_intended.json` and `rival.json`. This grid is task-lawful but deliberately outside the generator’s documented different-size construction; the generic target exposes no validator. The public Racket apply command is unsupported for this generic dynamic-program generator (exit 1, retained console), so this counterexample is Python-mirror evidence rather than an authoritative Racket receipt.

**Suggested repair:** generate same-size/different-shape odd objects often enough that each training lesson refutes size uniqueness, and add an executable size-only competitor. I did not edit this unrelated target.
